text:
maria: Quick sync — I ran a focused sweep for max_tokens_per_batch across A10/T4/L4/A100/H100 with KV-cache stress and varying kernel selectors. Results are non-linear: kernel choice + KV growth changes the optimal token budget by >2x in some cases. TL;DR table below and a proposal for defaults + queue policy tweak. Please review.
maria: Current observed (small sample, seq len 512/1024/2048):
```
GPU   VRAM  max_tokens_candidate  p50(ms)@512  p95(ms)@1024  throughput(tok/s)  notes
T4    16GB  32 / 64 / 96          45           120           18k                KV memory cliff >64
A10   24GB  64 / 128 / 192        30            85           35k                steady until 256
L4    16GB  48 / 96 / 144         28            70           30k                kernel fallback noisy
A100  40GB  128 / 256 / 384       20            50           60k                good fused kernels
H100  80GB  256 / 512 / 768       18            40           120k               register pressure at 768+
```
```
Note: p95 includes queueing under 95th percentile arrival bursts; measurements use continuous-batching runtime with prefix caching enabled.
```
maria: Proposal (defaults we check into configs):
- T4: max_tokens_per_batch = 48, max_concurrent_batches = 3
- A10: = 128, max_concurrent_batches = 4
- L4: = 96, max_concurrent_batches = 4, prefer safer kernel path when seq>1024
- A100: = 256, max_concurrent_batches = 6
- H100: = 512, max_concurrent_batches = 8

And queue policy change: token-budget-first (stop forming new batches when pending_token_budget < threshold) instead of count-first. Threshold = 1.5x median request length per GPU tier.

ryan: +1 on token-budget-first. Observed on T4 we hit an OOM more often because count-first packed many long seqs together. Also, KV cache for decoding grows per-request (seq * hidden) — we should cap per-request kv allocations in the allocator when below critical mem.

anika: L4 note — kernel selector picks the fast fused attention at seq<=1024 but flips to a safer matmul path for longer sequences. That's why p95 jumps around with mixed traffic. Suggest we bias selector to safer path when batch contains mixed seq lengths (heterogeneous batches).

jon: perf-bot flagged a regression when we enabled the new fused-kv kernel on A10; p95 climbed for 1024 in some runs. We should gate fused-kv with a Canary flag per GPU. See quick snippet for config override:
```
{ "gpu_profiles": {
  "A10": { "max_tokens_per_batch": 128, "enable_fused_kv": false, "canary_enable": true },
  "H100": { "max_tokens_per_batch": 512, "enable_fused_kv": true }
}}
```

sre-bot: FYI queue policy change could affect latency SLOs for small consumers — please add a rollout plan with metric guards: p95 latency, OOM count, tail queue length. Rollout steps: 10% -> 50% -> 100% per region with auto-rollback on 15% p95 regression.

perf-bot: Full profiling traces uploaded: https://perf.internal/redwood/sweeps/1912345678 — contains nvprof + runtime traces, kernel timelines, and KV allocation heatmaps. Quick summary: fused-kv decreases raw throughput by ~5% on A10 at seq=1024 but reduces CPU scheduling jitter; on H100 fused-kv + 512 tokens increases throughput ~12% but raises register divergence cases.

ryan: For the allocator change, we can implement a soft cap: when per-gpu free_vram < 1.2GB, limit per-request kv pages to floor(default_kv_pages * 0.6). This prevents sudden OOMs while allowing long requests to proceed at reduced batching priority.

anika: Also propose a micro-batching heuristic: if a batch contains >30% long-seq requests (>1024), split into two batches rather than fallback kernels. That reduces mixed-kernel noise.

maria: Action items: 1) Ryan - patch allocator soft cap + add unit test by EOD. 2) Jon - add canary flag for fused-kv per GPU, PR link in thread. 3) Anika - experiment with selector bias for mixed batches and micro-batching. 4) I'll open a rollout PR for token-budget-first queue policy with SLO guards. If no objections I'll land the default max_tokens_per_batch values tomorrow morning and start 10% rollout.

jon: small nit — set H100 max_concurrent_batches = 6 for now, 8 caused ioctl stalls in our infra test. I'll include that in the canary config.

maria: ack, will use 6 for H100. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: noted tests to monitor: runtime.p95_decode_ms, runtime.oom_count, runtime.queue_tail_ms

maria: I'll post PRs and the rollout plan once CI passes. Thanks for the fast feedback.
